leads.summary: The newline test passes even if newline rejection is removed
leads.consequence: The only newline case includes a complete '..' path component, so the independent */../* condition at bin/omarchy-refresh-config:24 rejects it even without the newline branch. Moreover no source directory named 'hypr\n' is planted, so the -e check at line 33 would reject it even with the entire lexical guard absent. This test does not protect the new newline-specific behavior. Plant a shipped source whose name contains a newline but no '..', pass that exact name, and assert the refusal message and absence of destination; optionally cover carriage return separately.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); corroborated. Adopted Sol nuance that a newline-only name would test the newline clause itself, supported by Opus mutant head_no_nl passing with planted dir.

leads.summary: Open PR #10413 changes the same guard, docs and test but expects a different refusal message
leads.consequence: Both proposals insert path guards at line 17 and append tests at line 38 of the common base. If #10413's version wins the guard, this PR's test fails for ../README and /etc/hosts because it requires 'Not a shipped user config' while #10413 emits 'Invalid config path'; if this PR's version wins, #10413's tests fail for the inverse reason. An integrator must reconcile the diagnostic and tests, not simply take both patches. Open PR #7992 also edits this command's backup/copy path and appends tests at the same line 38; its functionality appears compatible once the test append conflict is deliberately merged.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator via gh api (10413 patch emits 'Invalid config path'). Opus also noted #10413 overlap. Not published: cross-PR integration for maintainers, low value to this author; #12718 (same author, pre-fix copy) published instead.

limits: No code was run. Whole-string Bash pattern and missing fixture source establish H1 statically; repository source and read-only GitHub patches establish H2.
External PKGBUILDs were fetched from omacom/omarchy-pkgs master, whose _commit targets a released version, not this PR. They establish automatic bin/ shipping but not the future release contents.

HOME and OMARCHY_PATH are runtime environment premises, not validated by this change. Existing filesystem symlinks can redirect a lexical config path outside ~/.config; this is pre-existing behavior, and #10413 explicitly documents intentional dotfiles-symlink compatibility, not a newly introduced traversal bypass.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13214#issuecomment-5837637062), checked at `69a12f60` after the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13214#issuecomment-5841731875).

**Verified:** all four earlier points are resolved. One small gap remains in the new test case.

| Earlier point | Status at `69a12f60` |
|---|---|
| Newline in the argument skipped the `..` check | **Resolved.** The split is replaced by the whole-string `/$config_file/ == */../*` test, and `\n` and `\r` are also refused. With a `hypr<newline>` directory planted so the existence check passes, `hypr\n/../../README` is refused with no write; `ef782bc5` and base both write `$HOME/README`. |
| Stale `AGENTS.md` note | **Resolved.** The new sentence matches the behaviour. |
| Code comment on why absolute paths are refused | **Resolved.** It now gives the `/etc/hosts` → `~/.config/etc/hosts` case. |
| Unquoted redirection in the test | **Resolved.** With a `TMPDIR` containing a space, the test passes at this head and fails with "ambiguous redirect" at `ef782bc5`. |

**Verified:** the earlier results still hold. Absolute paths and every `..` form tried are refused with `Not a shipped user config: <arg>` and exit 1, and nothing is written. Legitimate relative paths still copy as on base (including `./hypr/hyprland.lua`, `hypr//hyprland.lua`, `hypr/..hidden.lua` and `hypr/my file.lua`). Every in-repository caller still passes a plain relative path. The only newly refused names are those containing a newline or `\r` anywhere (for example `hypr/a<newline>b.lua`, which `ef782bc5` and base copy). No caller uses such names. Results were the same with `extglob` and `nocasematch` inherited and under `LANG=C`.

**Optional test improvement:** the new newline case (`test/shell.d/refresh-config-test.sh`, lines 74-81) passes against every version of the script, including base with no guard at all. Nothing creates `$omarchy_path/config/hypr<newline>`, so the existing `[[ -e ]]` check would refuse the argument even without the new guard.

| Script | Case as shipped | With the directory planted |
|---|---|---|
| this head | passes | passes |
| `ef782bc5` (split-based guard) | passes | fails |
| base (no guard) | passes | fails |

Adding this line before the case makes it catch a return of the newline gap:

```bash
mkdir -p "$omarchy_path/config/hypr"$'\n'
```

Even then, the case passes with the separate newline clause removed, because its `..` also trips the whole-string check. A planted file such as `config/hypr/a<newline>b.lua` (newline inside the file name, no `..`) would cover that clause directly: with the clause removed it is copied.

**Optional wording:** the code comment (lines 22-23, "truncate a split-based scan") and the test comment (lines 74-75, "truncate the `..` scan") justify the newline refusal by a scan that the whole-string check no longer performs. The test comment also says "control characters", but only `\n` and `\r` are refused (a tab is accepted).

**Related PR:** open #12718 (same author) still contains byte-identical copies of the `ef782bc5` script and test, including the split-based guard and the unquoted redirection, and edits the same `AGENTS.md` paragraph. Syncing or dropping that part of #12718 would avoid bringing the newline gap back if both land.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of `69a12f60` against `ef782bc5` and the merge-base, plus sandboxed command-only runs of the script and `test/shell.d/refresh-config-test.sh` (as shipped and with the planted directory) against synthetic home and Omarchy trees (Bash 5.3). The full `test/shell` suite, routing through `bin/omarchy` and the migrations were not run. Related open PRs were checked only for overlapping files. Not tested on a live desktop.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
